note: Track barre (guitar-barre-chords), step 4: F and Bm reached on beat 1: from Am with a strum on every beat, faster in stages, from G, then F inside a four-chord round with the island strum.

exercise.title: Changes to a barre in time
exercise.why: A change to a barre comes late when your hand stays on the old chord until its last strum, so each block here asks for the barre on beat 1 with less time to get there.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat, a bar of Am and a bar of F.
When F lands on beat 1 with no gap, try a faster stage. Use the Stage selector below to change the tempo, then press Play to start the metronome again.
If F comes late at a new stage, leave out the last strum of the Am bar and use that beat to move.

Press Play below to start the metronome and strum down on every beat, a bar of G and a bar of Bm.
Let go of G on the last beat of its bar, so your hand is already moving when Bm is due.

Press Play below to start the metronome. The strokes in each box are the strum for the bar: play them through Am, F, C and G, a bar each.
Keep going until the F bar sounds as full as the other three.
